name: ebola_exposure
remarks: Ebola Exposure Assignment Submodule
Assigns contact type and checks ring-vaccination status before entering the
infection pathway. Contact type drives risk stratification and public-health
response documentation in downstream submodules.
Contact types per WHO case-contact definition:
household   — shared living space during infectious period (highest density)
healthcare  — HCW without adequate PPE (historically major amplification route)
funeral     — body-preparation or mourning contact (high-risk fluid exposure)
animal      — bushmeat handling or fruit-bat exposure (initial spillover only)
unknown     — epidemiologically unlinked; may represent unrecognized chains
Ring vaccination gate (Zaire only):
ERVEBO (rVSV-ZEBOV-GP) is recommended for Zaire ring vaccination.
Single-dose; WHO Guinea trial reported ~100% efficacy at 10 days post-vaccination.
If ebola_ring_vaccinated == true AND species == 'zaire', 85% of patients are
protected and exit without infection (15% vaccine breakthrough modeled).
No licensed reactive vaccine exists for Sudan or Bundibugyo species (2026).
Attributes read:   ebola_species, ebola_ring_vaccinated
Attributes set:    ebola_contact_type
References:
- WHO EVD fact sheet 2025; CDC EVD transmission page
- Guinea ring-vaccination trial (Lancet 2017); CDC vaccine use summary (SAGE 2020)
- WHO Bundibugyo expert consultation 2026 (no licensed reactive vaccine)
WHO/CDC outbreak data: household and funeral contacts predominate in community
outbreaks; HCW exposure was a major amplifier in 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic.
ERVEBO ring vaccination applies only to Zaire ebolavirus outbreaks.
For Sudan and Bundibugyo, no licensed reactive vaccine exists — proceed directly.
Vaccine protection modeled as 85% block on symptomatic disease after a
10-day protection window (SAGE recommendation; Guinea trial efficacy ~100%).
85% vaccine efficacy for ERVEBO against Zaire EVD (conservative estimate).
15% breakthrough infection — those continue to the infection pathway.
Non-breakthrough patients exit cleanly (protected, no clinical record).
